reviewer: Codex light owner, actual images inspected

views.name: hull_rig
findings: The preserved single lateen mast and sail have visible standing/running lines; the stowed anchor stock/flukes and aft tiller/rudder are actual separate fittings.
The honey-coloured planked hull has readable longitudinal grain, while its open well exposes frames and thwarts without an invented cabin or gun battery.
views.scope: Whole actual GLB with all visible hull, rig and sails.

views.name: deck_closeup
findings: At the matched 4.5 m field, separate staggered sole/platform boards have readable fine grain, narrow seams and real edge thickness; the construction is more articulated than the old Brig close-up.
Curved ribs, longitudinal bilge stringers, thwarts and knees remain exposed, with a real rope coil, iron-strapped tackle box, stowed oar and pierced outboard rig fittings visible.
views.scope: Actual deck and fitting close-up at a fixed 4.5 metre physical field; rig hidden for visibility.

views.name: open_bilge
findings: The open well exposes separate sole boards, curved ribs and longitudinal bilge stringers beneath real thwarts; there is no invented roof, enclosed room or painted black opening.
The rope coil, two planked tackle boxes and stowed oars have physical thickness and joinery. Rig is omitted as recorded while the hull, sole, frames and thwarts remain visible.
views.scope: Open boat well, exposed frames, bilge boards and thwarts; there is no enclosed cabin.

limitations: Static geometry and PBR inspection only; gameplay controllers and historical exactness are not certified.
The researched Tartane is an open boat: no enclosed hold or cabin is claimed. Its exposed timber construction and grain were compared with the old Brig deck close-up at the disclosed 4.5 m field.
The open-bilge and deck close-ups omit rig as recorded in the render manifest; hull, sole boards, frames, thwarts and fishing fittings remain actual delivered geometry.
